promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 5 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Keep the volume steady with one quality session and a steady long run, making recovery a priority.

flags.title: Easy HR share
flags.detail: keep heart rate under 150 for 80%+ of easy sessions

flags.title: Quality effort
flags.detail: keep the 9‑mile workout moderate and avoid over‑exertion

flags.title: Long run pace
flags.detail: watch the pace; stay at or below easy pace

flags.title: Recovery Sat
flags.detail: keep intensity low, focus on recovery

flags.title: Total mileage
flags.detail: aim for 40‑42 mi, check weekly total

answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, you don’t need to double‑up your mileage for a missed long run. Focus on maintaining the planned volume and quality. If you skip a session, add an easy run later to make up the miles.

new.analysis: The athlete is on build phase, 5 weeks to race. Keeping one quality session and a long run is appropriate. Add a Saturday easy run for recovery. The overall volume stays around 41-42 miles, about 80% easy. The flags focus on HR share, quality effort, long run pace, recovery, and total mileage. The question from earlier week about missed long run is answered, advising no need to double up but to add back a short easy run if desired. No safety concerns.
